    Proposition 2.1(2): the dual inequality gives a brick submodule #

    Let M be a finite-dimensional nonsimple brick over an algebraically closed field and S a one-dimensional simple module such that only finitely many kernels of epimorphisms M → S occur up to isomorphism (Remark 2.2). If dim Ext¹(S, M) < dim Hom(M, S), then M has a brick submodule of dimension dim M - 1 (exists_brick_submodule).

    The manuscript deduces part (2) from part (1) by the duality D. Here the argument is dualized directly: Step 1 applies kernel_polyCovered to the transposes of the inclusions ker g → M, and Step 2 uses the contravariant connecting inequality Ext1.finrank_hom_sub_le.

      Proposition 2.1(2). Over an algebraically closed field, let M be a finite-dimensional nonsimple brick and S a one-dimensional simple module such that only finitely many kernels of epimorphisms M → S occur up to isomorphism. If dim Ext¹(S, M) < dim Hom(M, S), then M has a brick submodule of dimension dim M - 1.
